text: Tom Regan's rights-based animal ethics differs from Peter Singer's chiefly in that Regan grounds moral status in...
choices: the capacity to suffer, aggregated within a utilitarian calculus of interests
membership in the biological species Homo sapiens
being a 'subject-of-a-life' with inherent value that cannot be traded off against aggregate utility
the possession of language and Kantian rational autonomy
explanation: Regan grounds status in being a subject-of-a-life (beliefs, desires, memory, a welfare), which confers inherent value resisting utilitarian trade-offs. The first option is Singer/Bentham's sentience utilitarianism; species membership is what both reject as speciesism; language and rationality is the personhood criterion Bentham set aside with 'Can they suffer?'
